timeline: While working as an IT specialist on the MOL Y2K project, Norbert Banhalmi began documenting the project on his own initiative with a basic 1.3-megapixel digital camera.
Information Engineering degree, followed by the founding of the Hungarian Defence Forces’ professional photo studio.
New York projects, major portrait exhibitions, NYIP studies, an applied-photographer qualification and three interdisciplinary books.
Becomes an Olympus—now OM SYSTEM—Ambassador; a permanent exhibition opens at the Csolnoky Ferenc Hospital Oncology Centre in Veszprém.
Co-founds and curates the digital Rege Gallery in Tihany; The Frame, NFT and AI projects examine how images change in digital culture.
Launches Hungarian-language photography education in Vienna and helps develop the community that later operates internationally as VIPACH.
Community portrait fundraisers support the Vienna Hungarian School’s climate-control and piano projects.
Joins AmCham Austria and the World Federation of Hungarian Photographers; launches the free Be Smart Kids Club for Hungarian-speaking young people aged 10–16.

exhibitions.name: Az igazi Nők / Real Women
exhibitions.summary: Natural beauty without digital correction; 30+1 portraits questioned the mythology of retouched perfection.

exhibitions.name: Régi kacér idők / The Good Old Flirty Days
exhibitions.summary: Pin-up was treated as attitude rather than costume, separating playful femininity from age and body norms.

exhibitions.name: Magyar nők New Yorkban / Hungarian Women in New York
exhibitions.summary: Urban portraiture connected Hungarian female identity with chosen places across New York.

exhibitions.name: A Nő ötven árnyalata / 50 Shades of Woman
exhibitions.summary: A deliberately varied emotional spectrum explored the distance between social role and inner state.

exhibitions.name: Apa lettem / I Became a Father
exhibitions.summary: Monochrome close studies dismantled stereotypes of masculinity through the intimate bond of father and child.

exhibitions.name: Mérföldkövek ’56 / Milestones ’56
exhibitions.summary: Portraits and personal objects gave individual faces to the historical trauma and resilience of 1956 émigrés.

exhibitions.name: Szösszenetek / Snippets
exhibitions.summary: Photography, poetry, video and performance formed an interdisciplinary dialogue with Vincent & Vincent.

exhibitions.name: Ébredés – az Új kezdet / Awakening
exhibitions.summary: Women living after gynaecological cancer were photographed with scars as signs of survival rather than deficit.

exhibitions.name: A Nő világa / The World of Woman
exhibitions.summary: Nine natural transitions in women’s lives were presented through personal testimony and portraiture.

exhibitions.name: Ballerina Project New York
exhibitions.summary: Movement, discipline and emotion were photographed outside the stage, between classical technique and urban space.
A group exhibition linking local and global identity through New York photographs representing Gödöllő.
exhibitions.name: Contemporary Artists of Pest County
The Frame — 20 Years
exhibitions.summary: Samsung The Frame became a changing digital exhibition surface for two decades of work.

exhibitions.name: Te is lehetsz… / You Can Be Too…
exhibitions.summary: A collaboration with the Hungarian National Ballet Institute focused on discipline, becoming and career choice.

exhibitions.name: The Men’s Dream
exhibitions.summary: Fine-art nude, NFT technology and a charity auction were combined to question authenticity in digital culture.

exhibitions.name: A valóság hamis arcai / The False Faces of Reality
exhibitions.summary: AI-generated portraits were used to provoke media literacy and distrust of technically perfect images.

exhibitions.name: Touch Vienna & Touch Munich
exhibitions.summary: Warm, gold-toned images presented tantra massage as holistic care and rehabilitated touch as a sacred human act.

exhibitions.name: Én a Nő / I Am the Woman
exhibitions.summary: A collective visual mosaic rejected a single definition of womanhood and anticipated the community logic of VIPACH.

exhibitions.name: Femme Fatale
exhibitions.summary: Lyrical softness and elemental strength were brought together in a collaborative reading of the archetype.

exhibitions.name: Más kép / Más / Different Image Different
exhibitions.summary: Photography in dialogue with Zsófia Szele’s poetry examined chronic illness, caregiving, resilience and love.
A twenty-work interdisciplinary project about unchoreographed presence and a tribute to Robert Capa’s ethos.
